sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Frauenfeld's parking debate is about how many public spaces the old town should keep. Ahead of the vote of 26 September 2021 the Stadtrat said it wants a revised parking regulation that sets fees so they steer traffic, not only recover costs, and put the city's special parking fund at just under CHF 6 million at the end of 2020 [0]. The authorities' own 2021 counts, as reported in the voting brochure, put the use of Parkhaus Altstadt at about 30% and of the Marktplatz garage at about 65%, while opponents of the credit said the Altstadt garage was mostly nearly empty and counted about 2,000 publicly accessible spaces in the inner city [2]. The city recorded a net loss of 42 public spaces in the centre over ten years, and 160 spaces north of the station were removed with 143 created at Unteres Mätteli [4]. In May 2022 voters were asked a CHF 11.3 million street-upgrade credit and 'Altstadt autofrei?', which would have meant pedestrian zones with no visitor parking; if rejected, a 20 km/h Begegnungszone with fewer parking spaces would apply on Freie-Strasse [5].

The argument is still live. In January 2026 an SVP councillor asked how many public spaces existed in 2020 and 2025, how many will remain at the end of 2027 and what revenue loss the Stadtrat expects; the answer was not found [6]. The city's August 2026 information on the inner-city street projects says some spaces on Promenade, Freie-Strasse and Rheinstrasse must be removed but will be replaced, partly through a swap with the canton; the plans were on exhibition until 2 September 2026, with building from 2027 subject to appeals [8]. Residents in four zones can buy a permit for CHF 30 a year [13].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The main development is the garage in the new cantonal government building. The Gemeinderat approved on 17 March 2021, by 25 votes to 14, a CHF 1.75 million credit to secure the public use of 50 of its 215 spaces; opponents used the referendum, which sent it to a public vote on 26 September 2021, and a later brochure refers to the rejection of the city's participation in the 50-space garage [3][5]. The canton expected the building to open around the end of 2024 or early 2025, and the 2021 brochure said about 40 spaces at Unteres Mätteli were expected to go for a cultural pavilion, with further reductions at Oberes Mätteli open [3][4]. The city's draft total revision of its parking-space regulation proposes raising the replacement levy for a missing car space from CHF 8,000 to CHF 10,000; it is a draft and not in force [7]. Three public charging stations with two 22 kW connectors each are listed in the city [15].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The city has 14 public car parks or garages, six of them city-owned [11]. Only two garages near the old town have public participation, according to the Stadtrat in 2021: the 63 public spaces in the Marktplatz building and Parkhaus Altstadt; Schlosspark, Passage and Haus am Bahnhof are privately run, and the city has no influence on their hours or tariffs [1]. Frauenfeld is notable for measuring occupancy: 24 cameras count it every two minutes at five car parks, with Parkhaus Altstadt added from September 2025 without cameras, paid for about half by the Zurich metropolitan region and half from the city's parking fund, with Parquery as technology partner [11]. The city approved an interim Smart Parking report on 18 August 2026; the pilot has been extended to the end of 2027, a final report is due in autumn 2027, and the data are meant to feed the revision of the parking regulation [9][10]. The Thurgau portal publishes the data every five minutes and warns that they are unvalidated measurements [12]. We do not hold current CHF tariffs.

Our data cover six areas with 555 spaces from that feed, measured since 26 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 40% on weekdays and 34% at weekends, weighted by spaces. The Oberes Mätteli (185) is the largest and fullest at 52% on weekdays, followed by Freie-Strasse/Bankplatz (30) at 54% and the Marktplatz 10-hour area (114) at 44%. All reached full or nearly full in single readings, including Unteres Mätteli on a Tuesday morning. Parkhaus Altstadt (66 spaces) is nearly empty, at 16% on weekdays and 7% at weekends, in line with the Altstadt garage that opponents described in 2021 [2]. The Marktplatz 10-hour area loses a third of its occupancy at weekends (44% to 30%), a commuter pattern. This is about four weeks of data.
